newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon Islamist killers executed by hanging.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon Islamist killers executed by hanging.

text.p: Three members of a radical Moslem group were executed by hanging early on Monday, more than two months after they were sentenced to death for killing a rival Islamist cleric in 1995, judicial sources said.

They said Munir Abboud, 25, Khaled Hamed, 27, and Ahmad al-Kasm, 25, were hanged before dawn at Roumyeh jail north of Beirut. The three members of Esbat al-Ansar faction, were sentenced to death on January 17 for the killing of Sheikh Nizar al-Halabi.
Their leader Palestinian Ahmed Saadi, believed to be hiding in Ain el-Hilweh Palestinian refugee camp near Sidon, was also sentenced to death in absentia.

Halabi, who headed the pro-Syrian Sunni group al-Ahbash, was gunned down in his car in mainly-Moslem West Beirut in August 1995. Saadi was convicted of ordering his killing and the three others of carrying it out.
Security sources said the Lebanese army tightened security around Ain el-Hilweh on Sunday and Monday for any possbile protests against the executions.
"It has been quiet so far inside the Ain el-Hilweh camp and outside," area residents said.

Lebanese President Elias Hrawi signed the death sentences, issued by Lebanon's highest court, the Judicial Council, on Friday. He rejected appeals by anti-Ahbash Islamist groups and clerics to commute the sentences against the three.
Beirut newspapers quoted on Monday a statement by the Meeting of Moslem Clerics as warning against the execution which "will mark the beginning of strife between Moslems".

The court had opened the trial of 20 Islamists, including Saadi and the three others, in May 1996 on charges of killing Halabi and belonging to a violent armed group. The remaining suspects were given life jail terms or shorter prison sentences.
